text:
sam: Heads up — noticed a ~12-18ms median bump on the host-side parse path in last night's canary (svc-alpha). Latency tail looks worse too.

linh: Saw that in dashboards; request parsing p95 jumped from ~35ms to ~60ms. Any recent changes to proto/unmarshal or writev coalescing? :thinking: 

maya: I pushed the proto change that unifies request header parsing to the host parser earlier this week (PR #4218). It landed in the build that rolled last night.

david: Can we get a flamegraph / perf profile from the canary? I suspect HPACK decode + small writev syscalls are dominating.

perf-bot: Collected profiles at 03:12Z from svc-alpha-canary (3 hosts). Upload: s3://perf-redwood/1752468000/profiles.tar.gz

sam: Quick grep of the flame shows heavy time in host::parse::hpack_decode and runtime::memcpy (small copies). Also notable kvcache evictions around the same window.

linh: Reproduced locally with a 40k sample replay. pprof output snippet:

Top functions (by samples):
  34.6%  host::parse::hpack_decode
  22.1%  runtime::memcpy
  10.5%  kvcache::shard::evict
   6.4%  grpc::stream::writev_emit
   4.2%  kernel_selector::choose_path

maya: Hmm — the proto unify moved some header normalization earlier, which may increase small-copy churn into the writev path. Did we change autoscaling for batching heuristics? Small batches increase write syscalls.

ciara: I instrumented request sizes. Canary had a surge of many short requests (avg 96 bytes) from a load test. Batching heuristics recently lowered the max-delay to 2ms to improve latency, which reduces batching opportunity.

sam: So two factors: more work in host parse (HPACK + header normalize) + fewer batching coalesces => more writev/syscall overhead and more KV cache pressure. That explains the p95 increase.

david: Quick experiment idea: revert header-normalize move in one canary host, and in another keep normalization but bump max-delay to 6ms to allow coalesce. Compare CPU and syscall counts.

maya: I can deploy a 1-host revert canary. Command I used to build the change:

make build-host-parser && ./deploy-canary --hosts=1 --tag=pr-4218-revert

linh: I'll run a focused perf trace (perf record -g -F 99) during the replay and capture strace -c to count writev/syscalls. Also pushing a micro-benchmark that sends many small requests.

perf-bot: Trace captures: /artifacts/1752468000/trace-host1.perf, /artifacts/1752468000/strace-host1.txt

ciara: KV cache metrics: during the spike we saw increased shard miss rate from 0.7% -> 4.9% and evictions up 3x. Likely due to less batching and different request key distribution after header normalization.

sam: Another angle — kernel selection step: profiler shows kernel_selector::choose_path costing ~4% but memory layout of buffers changed after the proto change so chosen kernel has worse mem-copy patterns. Could be AVX path hitting misaligned buffers.

david: For isolation, try forcing a different kernel (fallback) on the canary process: set env RUN_KERNEL=scalar and RUN_KERNEL=avx2 in separate runs. See perf delta.

maya: Will add a quick flag and roll two canaries. Also instrument a micro flamegraph for K/V hit paths.

linh: Preliminary strace counts from original canary (period sample):

% time  seconds  calls  errors syscall
27.1  0.123    23456  0      writev
18.4  0.083    23456  0      recvmsg
10.5  0.047     9876  0      write

That writev call count is very high.

ciara: If batching delay increase reduces writev calls by ~3x, kvcache hit rate improves and evictions drop — I ran a short local test. So change to batching heuristics might restore previous economics.

sam: Risks: bumping max-delay could raise tail latency for some customers. We need to A/B carefully and track per-model latency. Also header normalization revert might hide correctness/compatibility improvements.

david: Plan: (1) deploy two one-host canaries — revert parser change and increased batching delay. (2) Run 30min replay + production-mini-ramp. (3) Collect p95/p99, writev counts, kvcache evictions, kernel-profile. (4) Decide revert vs. kernel-layout fix vs. batching tuning.

maya: I'll own the revert canary and the follow-up PR with a trimmed header-normalize that avoids extra copies. Target: patch by EOD and canary by 02Z.

linh: I'll coordinate perf captures and prepare dashboards for quick comparison. cc @ciara for kvcache metrics.

ciara: Adding dashboards: /dashboards/host-parse/1752468000-compare. Alerting rule temporarily on writev counts > 15k/min.

sam: Thanks all. If either canary makes numbers look good, we'll roll the fix across canaries and consider a conservative batching default until kernel/layout changes land. :thumbsup:

ciara: Note — add a regression test that replays micro-bursty short requests in CI to prevent reintroducing this.

perf-bot: Next steps logged: ticket RED-3175 created for follow-up (owner: maya).
